dedupe_keys.name: dlr ionosphere monitoring and prediction center impc

description: The Ionosphere Monitoring and Prediction Center (IMPC) of the German Aerospace Center provides space weather services on the state of the ionosphere for aviation, space flight, shipping and ground transport, because ionospheric variability and disturbances degrade the accuracy, reliability and availability of satellite navigation, communication and remote sensing radio systems. Its products include total electron content maps and forecasts, and ionospheric perturbation indices such as the Rate of Change of TEC Index, equivalent slab thickness, Swarm-based gradient indices (NEGIX and TEGIX), local scintillation measurements and the Disturbance Ionosphere indeX spatial gradients, alongside news such as a 2026 survey of space weather impacts on aviation operations. It covers the current state and forecasts of the ionosphere. It is run by the Department for Space Weather Impact of DLR's Institute for Solar-Terrestrial Physics in Neustrelitz, and the SWEET project is developing new interactive tools for it. Products are available free on the website; DLR holds copyright in the content and reuse needs permission under the IMPC terms of use. Caveats: maintenance can interrupt services, and the terms restrict reuse without a licence. It supports hazard exposure and service performance analysis of GNSS, HF communication and aviation systems during space weather; a related record is the DLR GNSS Performance Monitoring website.
